item_side.rule: Unless a weapon lists SECONDARY in its slot list it cannot be held in the offhand.
item_side.source: the owner, directly, 28 Aug 2026 — it invalidated a published ranking of mine that paired two PRIMARY-only swords
item_side.b_already_has_this: B reports `slot` as resolvable, so B can apply this without me. 424 of 788 weapon items are SECONDARY-capable; 224 are PRIMARY-only.
item_side.b_query_rerun: B ran 'items with a 2H skill that also list SECONDARY' and got 0, correctly calling it vacuous because no item carries a skill. Re-run here where skill IS present: still 0, and NOT vacuous — 124 two-handers exist in this corpus to have been caught. The reassuring fact B wanted is real.

class_side.status: DO NOT SHIP AS A GATE
class_side.why_not: This session's own audit (BRIEF-eqlsource.md) concluded: 'the rule is inherited from classic EverQuest and is unmeasured on Legends... Do not add a dual-wield class gate; the geometric rule is safe and the class rule is genuinely unsettled.' No log in 138 shows a two-handed primary, and eqlwiki's Dual Wield section presumes the rule without stating it.
class_side.and_against_me: model4.py line 50 uses this set as a hard gate anyway, which is my own brief's advice ignored in my own model. Recorded, not quietly fixed.
class_side.what_to_do_instead: A dismissible banner, not a hard block, saying the class restriction is inherited from classic EverQuest and unmeasured on Legends.
class_side.what_would_settle_it: One log, or one client screenshot, of a non-dual-wield class attempting to equip a SECONDARY weapon.
